sentences.text: Saltasaurus holds the distinction of being the first sauropod genus known to possess armor made of bony plates embedded in its skin.
Although relatively small among sauropods, this animal was still huge by human standards and possessed a head similar to that of diplodocids.
Its back featured a series of bony plates and nodules along the dorsal region, featuring prominent bony spines.
The creature possessed armor similar to a crocodile, with osteoderms measuring 10 to 12 centimeters in diameter.
Estimates suggest the animal was approximately 12 meters long and weighed an estimated 7 tons.
The discovery of Saltasaurus eggs embedded in nesting grounds suggests gregarious nesting behavior as a protection and survival strategy with high offspring rates.
Hundreds of female Saltasaurus dug holes with their hind legs, laid eggs in clutches averaging around 25, and buried the nests under ground and vegetation.
Small eggs, about 11 to 12 centimeters in diameter, contained fossilized embryos with skin impressions showing a mosaic armor of small bead-like scales.
Fossils of Saltasaurus were excavated by José Bonaparte, Martín Vince, and Juan C. Leal between 1975 and 1977 at the Estancia El Brete.
Saltasaurus was named and described by Bonaparte and Jaime E. Powell in 1980.
The original discovery was made in the late 1970s and consisted of a group of six incomplete skeletons.
The fossils were found in the Balbuena subgroup of the Salta Group within the El Brete Formation.
Saltasaurus was herbivorous, like all sauropods.
Previously, it was assumed that size alone was sufficient defense for sauropods.
Since then, paleontologists have investigated the possibility that other sauropods also had armor, such as Laplatasaurus.
Powell assumed adult Saltasaurus were protected by body armor while juveniles were protected by the herd.
Powell suggested that Saltasaurus was aquatic.
Saltasaurus belongs to the family Saltasauridae, which was previously called Titanosauridae but was redefined with Saltasaurus as the type genus due to inaccuracies in known remains.
Loricosaurus scutatus is a possible synonym of Saltasaurus.
Armor plates previously named as Loricosaurus by Friedrich von Huene are now suggested to belong to Saltasaurus rather than an ankylosaurian.
While relationships within Titanosauria remain highly controversial, most studies agree that Saltasaurus is one of the most derived titanosaur genera.
Saltasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 73 and 66 million years ago, in what is now South America.
Saltasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Saltasaurus was one of those titanosaurid sauropods that lived about 70 million years ago.

Saltasaurus proved that titanosaurs were the dominant fauna in South America during the Late Cretaceous, contradicting the view that hadrosaurs like Edmontosaurus displaced primitive sauropods globally as they did in Laurasia.

Since bony armor was previously known only in thyreophorans, Saltasaurus demonstrated that massive sauropods did not need additional protection, helping to reclassify armored finds like Titanosaurus from nodosaurids.
